rules.statement: A deed of transfer that is executed contrary to law is null and void.
rules.supporting_quote: (1) The Deed of Transfer was executed contrary to law and therefore of no effect in law being null and void. (2) Defendant-appellant's long possession does not give him any prescriptive rights - S. 161. (3) Since the Deed of transfer was ab-initio void, the defendant-appellant is not entitled to get the benefit of the equitable principle of estoppel. 368 (4) Even if the plaintiff-respondent committed a fraud he could not be called upon to give title to something over which he had no right of alienation
